title: Running Up That Hill — Meaning, Genes, And Nothing Else #Shorts
description:
The selfish-gene reading of Running Up That Hill makes it less romantic and far more precise. "Running Up That Hill" (also titled "Running Up That Hill (A Deal with God)") is a song by the English singer-songwriter Kate Bush, released as the lead single from her fifth studio album, Hounds of Love, on 5 August 1985 by EMI Records. Bush wrote and produced it using a Fairlight CMI synthesiser and a LinnDrum drum machine.

Behind Running Up That Hill sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. The American rock band Faith and the Muse included a goth-style cover of "Running Up That Hill" on the 2001 compilation album Vera Causa. The British rock band Placebo included a version of "Running Up That Hill" on their 2003 compilation album Covers, which reached number 44 on the UK singles chart.
